_readme: THE DEFINITION of what a member of staff's assistant may do on an organisation
box (org_mode on, src/lib/org-mode.ts). No second copy of this table exists;
JSON because its readers are four languages:
src/lib/org-staff-policy.ts                     the agent roster and the Hermes profile (TypeScript)
scripts/org-staff-policy.js                     the user relay's slash-command filter (CommonJS)
An ALLOW-list on both runtimes, like org-mode.ts: a tool the core or a plugin
adds later is the owner's until it is named here. The owner keeps everything;
a home box (org_mode off) never reads this file.
_agentPrefix: Each member of staff has their OWN agent on OpenClaw (agents.entries.<prefix><name>)
and their OWN profile on Hermes (~/.hermes/profiles/<prefix><name>): their own
workspace, memory files, memory index, sessions and skills. Usernames are
[a-z_][a-z0-9_-]{0,31} (src/lib/username-rules.ts), so the id is at most 46
characters — inside both cores' [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63} id rule.
_mcpEntryPrefix: The MCP servers the owner lets members of staff use (Settings -> System -> Users,
src/lib/staff-mcp.ts) reach each member's agent as an OpenClaw mcp.servers entry
of its own, named <prefix><8 hex of the username>-<server>, pointing at ClawBox's
loopback relay with THAT member's relay token. The member's agent gets
<entry>__* in its tools.allow; clawbox-staff-guard lets a staff agent call only
the entries granted to it (staff-mcp-grants.json beside the plugin) and refuses
every other agent's call to one. Never clawbox__*. Hermes staff get none.
_slashCommands: The only slash commands a member of staff may send: a fresh conversation and
the reasoning switch. /model, /config, /restart, /bash and every other command
or inline directive is refused before it reaches the runtime.
_openclaw: allow: the per-agent tools.allow of every staff agent (core tool ids). File
tools are further held to the member's own folder by clawbox-staff-guard.
deny: written beside it so the intent survives a widened allow — deny always
takes sub-agents and cross-session sends, group:automation cron, gateway,
plugins and the setup helper, group:ui the browser and the terminal,
group:messaging every outbound channel, clawbox__* the device's MCP tools.
writeTools may only touch the member's folder; readTools may also read the
_hermes: toolsets: platform_toolsets.cli of every staff profile — the dashboard builds
a session's agent from it (tui_gateway/agent_factory.py). disabledToolsets:
agent.disabled_toolsets, which Hermes applies last and which also strips the
client-surface toolsets the desktop folds in. allowTools is what
clawbox_staff_guard lets a staff profile's turn call at all; writeTools may only
touch the member's folder, readTools may also read the staged attachments.
